assessment.summary: The scan supports central network-admission ownership and explicit rooted-filesystem capabilities; focused variants are recommended for v0.7.

nonNegotiables: Preserve loopback REST, MCP, Wails, authenticated peer sync, large snapshots, and tolerant legacy imports.
Do not add general authentication or a second listener during v0.7 release closure.
assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
Reverse proxies and unauthenticated remote ordinary APIs are unsupported.
The explicitly selected archive or carrier root is a trusted mount or alias.

opportunities.title: Own network admission in one lifecycle boundary
opportunities.summary: Make connection authority, transport selection, browser origin, and byte admission explicit before application mutations.
opportunities.diagnosis: A shared listener granted access to the full mux while transport and admission controls were distributed across executables and handlers.

evidence.claim: The remote-capable server attached the full ordinary and peer handler.
Desktop serving bypassed configured TLS selection.
Unsafe browser requests lacked central origin admission.
Ordinary JSON, MCP, and resource admission lacked shared ceilings.
Connection and transport policy belongs to the service lifecycle; browser and body policy belongs to shared HTTP/store admission.

desiredInvariants: Only finite peer-sync endpoints are remotely reachable; ordinary endpoints require a loopback peer and local Host.
Every executable uses one TLS selector and partial TLS starts no listener.
Unsafe browser requests and admitted bytes pass exact centralized bounds before mutation.

options.title: Central listener guard
options.summary: Keep one listener and centralize network/TLS admission while retaining HTTP/store origin and byte controls.

findingCoverage.rationale: The finite remote mux and loopback/Host check are the tactical boundary.
The shared Service serving selector removes executable drift.
Central unsafe-method origin admission is retained.
Shared exact-one JSON plus HTTP/store resource ceilings remain necessary.

tradeoffs.assessment: Remote and local route authority is checked before the full mux.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise real remote/local peers, spoofed forwarding headers, and unknown sync paths.

tradeoffs.assessment: Admission adds constant address, Host, route, and bounded-decode work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare REST and peer request latency/throughput before and after.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only bounded request state and decoder buffers are introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare loaded peak RSS under maximum accepted bodies.

tradeoffs.assessment: One transport selector eliminates executable lifecycle drift.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject partial/unreadable TLS pairs in every command mode.

tradeoffs.assessment: One endpoint remains, but proxy exclusions and denials need documentation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run operator SSH-tunnel and non-loopback deployment exercises.

tradeoffs.assessment: No stored data, peer URL, or configuration migration is required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run existing profile and peer compatibility suites.

residualRisks: A loopback reverse proxy is unsupported.
Future peer endpoints must be added to the finite remote mux deliberately.

acceptanceCriteria: Remote ordinary routes fail while peer sync and loopback clients remain compatible.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable remote sync and bind loopback before reverting focused changes.

options.title: Split local and peer listeners
options.summary: Register ordinary and peer route families on distinct typed listener profiles.

findingCoverage.rationale: Socket separation removes remote ordinary registration; bind checks remain.
Both listeners still need centralized transport lifecycle.
A hostile browser can still reach the local socket.
Admitted local and peer clients still require body ceilings.

tradeoffs.assessment: Route-family authority becomes structural at socket registration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory registered routes and test both sockets from local/remote peers.

tradeoffs.assessment: No extra request hop is required, but connection pools split.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark concurrent ordinary and peer workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: A second server, listener, and connection pool retain state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare idle and loaded RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failure isolation improves, but partial startup becomes a new state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject bind, certificate, and shutdown failures independently.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators manage two addresses, health views, and firewall rules.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run upgrade and incident exercises.

tradeoffs.assessment: Configuration, peer URLs, documentation, and compatibility behavior change.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test old-profile upgrade, mixed peer versions, and rollback.

residualRisks: Origin and body admission remain mandatory.
General remote APIs still need general authentication.

acceptanceCriteria: Ordinary routes are absent from the peer socket and peer routes are absent from the local socket.
migrationNotes: Retain the shared-listener guard until every profile migrates.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Return profiles to the guarded shared listener.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the central guard for v0.7; choose split listeners when remote ordinary/proxy operation becomes a supported product requirement.

opportunities.title: Keep untrusted trees behind explicit root capabilities
opportunities.summary: Replace ambient descendant paths with rooted, descriptor-validated, bounded operations.
opportunities.diagnosis: Carrier and legacy archive code validated names but retained ambient filesystem authority after string path joins.

evidence.claim: Carrier reads, writes, removals, fallbacks, and snapshots followed hostile descendants or special files.
Legacy archive consumed entries followed descendants and discovered resources late.
Root containment is common, while carrier resume and archive preflight remain distinct domain policies.

desiredInvariants: Every descendant operation is relative to one pinned selected root.
Consumed entries are regular, identity-checked, and bounded by per-file, aggregate, and scan ceilings.
Writable carrier partials/fallbacks cannot modify carrier-provided hardlinked outside inodes.
Legacy resource import consumes its preflight inventory without hostile re-enumeration.

options.title: Subsystem-owned rooted access
options.summary: Keep rooted descriptor helpers and lifecycle limits with the carrier and archive owners.

findingCoverage.rationale: Rooted carrier operations, bounded iteration, and writable-link checks are the tactical fix.
Rooted aggregate preflight and one resource inventory are the tactical fix.

tradeoffs.assessment: Ambient descendant authority is replaced by package-owned root capabilities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run link, special-file, race, growth, cardinality, and aggregate mutation suites.

tradeoffs.assessment: Descriptor identity adds metadata operations; bounded batches prevent pathological allocation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Profile valid large carrier and 382k-note archive workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Directory batches and explicit inventory ceilings bound attacker-controlled allocation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS for valid and invalid maximum inventories.

tradeoffs.assessment: Special files and unsafe trees fail deterministically before blocking or persistence.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject FIFO, path swaps, file growth, and device removal.

tradeoffs.assessment: No service is added; new refusal messages and platform limitations require documentation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review operator-visible errors on supported filesystems.

tradeoffs.assessment: On-disk layout and accepted valid archive/carrier formats remain unchanged.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run round-trip, removable-media, non-atomic, ignored-sidecar, and large-resource tests.

residualRisks: Trusted-root bind mounts and read-only hardlinks remain explicit assumptions.
Concurrent hostile mutation is not transactional.
Plan 9 and js Root semantics are unsupported.

acceptanceCriteria: Unsafe entries fail within declared bounds before outside writes or canonical import mutation.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop using the suspect tree and restore from a trusted copy; reverting checks is not a safe operational rollback.

options.title: Shared safe-root capability
options.summary: Centralize typed regular-read, single-link-write, and bounded-directory capabilities with platform policy.

findingCoverage.rationale: Carrier domain checks remain while low-level operations migrate.
Archive aggregate and preflight policy remains in its adapter.

tradeoffs.assessment: New consumers inherit one reviewed descriptor order, but a shared bug has larger blast radius.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fuzz and mutation-test the capability and each adapter.

tradeoffs.assessment: Expected I/O is similar; iterator and interface mechanics are unmeasured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark identical trees against package-local helpers.

tradeoffs.assessment: Typed iterators preserve bounded batches; adapter inventories remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare allocations and peak RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Platform behavior becomes consistent, but one defect affects every consumer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run cross-platform fault matrices before migration.

tradeoffs.assessment: One platform-policy inventory is easier to audit; errors must retain domain context.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review logs and support diagnostics from both adapters.

tradeoffs.assessment: Two callers and platform helpers migrate while tactical paths coexist.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Stage read-only then writable operations with source-search gates and rollback adapters.

residualRisks: A generic API can hide domain-specific state transitions.
Bind-mount policy still requires a supported-platform decision.

acceptanceCriteria: All ambient descendant operations are absent and both domain suites preserve compatibility.
migrationNotes: Retain package-local helpers until all capability tests and source audits pass.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Select the retained package-local implementation without changing on-disk data.

opportunities.recommendation: Keep subsystem-owned rooted access for v0.7; centralize after a third consumer or stronger cross-platform link policy appears.

openQuestions: Will v0.8 support reverse proxies or authenticated general remote access?
Are in-root bind mounts and read-only hardlinks in the supported threat model?
Which platforms must certify identical no-follow and link-count behavior?
